verifiedAgainst: CEN/TC 434 eInvoicing EN 16931 validation artefacts, release 1.3.16
description: The business rules of EN 16931-1, clause 6.4, and the decimal and code list restrictions the validation artefacts derive from clauses 6.5.12 and 6.3, written over semantic paths so that one rule serves a UBL invoice, a CII invoice and a document that was never XML alike. Every rule statement is taken from the norm text and written in this project's own words; no expression and no assertion text of the CEN artefacts is translated or copied, and the artefacts stay the authority. Where the statement of the standard admits more than one reading — a tolerance, a rounding — the rule follows the artefacts, because that is what the ecosystem validates against, and says so in its note; where the two artefacts read it differently, it faults from the wider of their readings on and reports a warning, which decides no verdict, inside the zone only one of them grants, naming the syntax whose artefact faults a figure there, so that it never faults a figure the artefact of the document's own syntax accepts. Where an artefact's expression cannot fire at all, the rule follows the norm and reports; conformance/rules/ledger.md names those. The coverage table in conformance/rules/coverage.md says which rule of the release is implemented here, which is about the XML binding and therefore invisible to this engine, and which is deferred and why.
